summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every Hindi video gets 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 50. The best videos use a surprising 'it doesn't see/hear/think the way you expect' angle on simple, relatable devices like gyro robots, clap switches and motion sensors. Longer 'How does X work?' titles on public-place gadgets (lift, mall door, tap, smoke alarm) get far fewer views, likes and saves.
winningPattern: Hindi videos on hobby-robot or maker-style sensors (gyro, clap switch, PIR, line follower, mic) with a counterintuitive, short statement hook such as 'X doesn't do the obvious thing, it does the opposite' or 'Without X, this falls instantly'. Titles are punchy statements, not 'how does it work' questions, with one emoji and #shorts. Instagram Reels is the main driver, and the best videos from Oct 29 to Nov 5 reached 1,200 to 1,400 views with strong likes and saves. YouTube only works when the video also has a strong hook (Gyro, Clap Switch, PIR reached 550 to 680 views).
doMore: Make robot and maker-project topics (balance, line following, obstacle avoidance) with a 'robot has no brain/eyes' twist hook
Use bold counterintuitive statements as titles and first lines instead of 'Kaise kaam karta hai?' questions
Do follow-up videos on the Clap Switch and Gyro themes, since those got the most saves and views on both platforms
End with a save-worthy takeaway (a pin diagram, a one-line rule, a part name) to boost saves and shares
Keep posting daily on Instagram first, and re-test on YouTube using the winning hook styles to grow it
stopDoing: Generic public-place gadget explainers like lift, mall door, washroom tap, which stay under 600 views
Near-duplicate topics (smoke alarm x2, IR sensor in dark, tap x2) that split the audience and underperform
Question-style titles starting with 'Kaise...? 🤔' as the default format
nextTopics: Obstacle avoiding robot with ultrasonic sensor
